request.spec:
A steward can re-settle a SETTLED claim (anyone else, or any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim). Re-settling freezes the claim again at the figure
it would have today as an open claim bound by no statement: today's rates, grades, floor and late
charge. The status log gains a SETTLED line for it, and CLAIM_RESETTLED is written, naming the
claim like every claim line, ending old=<previous figure> new=<new figure>.

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can re-settle a SETTLED claim (anyone else, or any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim). Re-settling freezes the claim again at the figure
it would have today as an open claim bound by no statement: today's rates, grades, floor and late
charge. The status log gains a SETTLED line for it, and CLAIM_RESETTLED is written, naming the
claim like every claim line, ending old=<previous figure> new=<new figure>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Stewards can now re-settle a settled claim, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Server**
- **New rule** (`ClaimService.resettle`): only a steward can re-settle, only a SETTLED claim, and not one dated in a closed period. Anything else is refused and changes nothing.
- **How the new figure is worked out** (`RollupService.openDueOf`): the claim is priced as an open claim bound by no statement. That means the rate its grade has in force on the claim's date, raised to the floor, plus whatever late charge it would carry today. The claim keeps its "stated" flag; this only changes the figure it is frozen at.
- **Status log and audit:** re-settling adds a `SETTLED by <user> on <today> due=<new>` line to the status log. It writes `CLAIM_RESETTLED … old=<previous> new=<new>` to the audit file, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines when the totals move.
- **Endpoint:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{id}/resettle`, in `ClaimController`.

**Front end**
- Each claim row has a new `claim-resettle` button. A refusal shows on the row's existing `claim-error`, with its own message for not a steward, not settled, closed period, or claim gone.

**Behaviour to be aware of**
- Re-settling still goes through when the new figure equals the old one; one of the scenarios expects exactly this (`old=0.50 new=0.50`).
- If no rate applies, the claim is frozen at `n/a` rather than refused, the same as an ordinary settle does today. The tests don't cover this case.

No database migration was needed: re-settling reuses the claim's existing settled-due field and status log.
